title: Mandeep Singh Hat-Trick Powers India To 13-0 Rout Of Bangladesh In Jalandhar
excerpt: Harmanpreet, Dilpreet and Hardik scored twice each as the defending champions led 6-0 at half-time in their Asian Champions Trophy opener on October 27.
body:
• India beat Bangladesh 13-0 in Jalandhar on October 27 to open their Asian Champions Trophy title defence, with Mandeep Singh scoring in the 3rd, 10th and 54th minutes.
  • Captain Harmanpreet Singh, Dilpreet Singh and Hardik Singh scored twice each, with Shilanand Lakra, Abhishek, Nilakanta Sharma and Jugraj Singh adding one goal each.
  • India led 4-0 after the first quarter and 6-0 at half-time, then scored three goals in the 43rd and 44th minutes to put the result beyond doubt.
  • Nilakanta Sharma announced he will retire from international hockey after this tournament, and India next face China on October 29.

India opened the defence of their Asian Champions Trophy title with a 13-0 win over Bangladesh at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar on Tuesday, October 27, as Mandeep Singh scored a hat-trick and eight different Indian players found the net.

Mandeep completed his hat-trick in the 3rd, 10th and 54th minutes. Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored in the 2nd and 44th minutes, Dilpreet Singh in the 43rd and 44th, and Hardik Singh twice in the 60th minute. Shilanand Lakra (15th), Abhishek (18th), Nilakanta Sharma (26th) and Jugraj Singh (46th) were the other scorers, IANS reported.

A fast start that Bangladesh could not answer

India earned a penalty corner in the second minute and Harmanpreet converted it with a drag-flick. A minute later Mandeep collected a pass from Harmanpreet at the top of the circle and scored with a reverse hit. Bangladesh had a chance in the fourth minute, but Lakra cleared the ball. Mandeep scored again in the 10th minute from close range after Harmanpreet's aerial ball found Abhishek, who played it into the circle, and Lakra made it 4-0 in the 15th minute after a move involving Sukhjeet Singh and Aditya Arjun Lalage.

The second quarter followed the same pattern. Abhishek made it 5-0 in the 18th minute after receiving a pass from Mandeep on the left. Bangladesh goalkeeper Ashraful Shad made a save against Nilakanta, but Nilakanta scored in the 26th minute with a reverse-stick shot from the top of the circle to give India a 6-0 half-time lead. RevSportz described the finish as a superb tomahawk and noted the match was played in front of a packed stadium, 17 years after international hockey last took place in Punjab.

Three goals in two minutes end the contest

Bangladesh held the ball for longer spells in the third quarter, but India scored three times at its close. Dilpreet converted a penalty corner in the 43rd minute and scored again from open play a minute later. Harmanpreet then converted another penalty corner in the 44th minute to make it 9-0. Jugraj converted a penalty corner in the 46th minute, Mandeep completed his hat-trick in the 54th by stretching to turn in a cross from Aditya, and Hardik scored twice in the final minute, the second after Harmanpreet found Dilpreet, who laid the ball off for him.

The result put India top of the standings after the opening day with three points and a goal difference of +13. In the other matches, Malaysia beat China 5-4 and Japan defeated South Korea 3-2. The six-team tournament is played in a single round-robin format, with each team playing the other five once and the top four qualifying for the semi-finals.

What it means and what comes next

The margin gives the defending champions early control of the league stage, but the scoreline came against the weakest resistance they are likely to face in Jalandhar. The more significant tests are still to come in the round-robin, starting with China. The evening also carried a personal milestone: Nilakanta announced his retirement from international hockey, with this tournament his last appearance in an India jersey, IANS reported.

India next face China on October 29 at 1900 IST. October 28 is a rest day. All league matches will be played in Jalandhar until November 2, before the tournament moves to the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali for the semi-finals on November 4 and the bronze-medal and gold-medal matches on November 5.
